title: Simon King · professional profile

title: Department for Speech, Music and Hearing
note: Use the department’s speech communication research pages to trace questions about production, perception and interaction back to experiments.

title: Research at the Centre for Speech Technology Research
note: The centre’s research archive connects acoustic measurements, synthesis and evaluation. Follow project dates and use the linked papers for specific results.

title: Kyutai · open-science AI lab
note: Pair the lab’s speech demos with the papers and corresponding code. A short demo demonstrates behavior on one interaction.

title: Generic Indic Text-to-Speech Synthesisers with Rapid Adaptation in an End-to-End Framework
by: Anusha Prakash and Hema A. Murthy
note: Examine the within-language-family transfer design and how the authors assessed adaptation to a target language. Keep speaker identity, language membership and data quantity separate in a replication.

title: Measuring the Cognitive Load of Synthetic Speech Using a Dual Task Paradigm
note: Read the unexpected result involving natural speech before interpreting secondary-task reaction time as a pure measure of effort. The study compares several synthesizers with natural recordings.

title: ESPnet · End-to-End Speech Processing Toolkit
note: Trace the recipe from data preparation to scoring. Use a matching historical recipe before comparing the paper’s results with the evolving repository.

title: Data and tools related to the Blizzard Challenge
note: Find listening-test tools, results and audiobook datasets. Availability and reuse conditions differ by challenge year and corpus.

title: Praat · doing phonetics by computer
note: Use the manual and scripting tools to extract reproducible acoustic measurements. Report window and pitch settings when comparing speakers.

title: Contributing to SpeechBrain
note: The maintainers describe contribution types, runnable documentation and tests. A small reproducible example can be prepared locally under their conventions.

title: Automatic Speech Recognition of Conversational Speech in Individuals with Disordered Speech
note: Read the paired read/conversational comparison across 27 participants, including personalized models. The population and tasks limit transfer to a different user or device.

title: Personalized Automatic Speech Recognition Trained on Small Disordered Speech Datasets
note: Study the relationship between per-speaker data quantity and success criteria. The authors evaluate selected scenarios and report substantial variation across speakers.
